title: Fixed-size pool, OOM policy, fragmentation numbers
objective: Implement a pool of M fixed-size blocks with documented OOM and double-free results, prove the pool can refill after a full free, and publish a measurement of pool bytes versus a scripted allocation pattern.
whyThisMatters: A 'custom allocator' that cannot say what happens at M+1 or on double-free is still a heap with extra steps. Edge firmware needs a pool whose failure modes are tests, not crashes.
evidence: Pool C sources and a test program with incremental Git history
A captured run showing alloc M+1 returning the documented OOM result after M successes
A captured run showing double-free of the same block returning the documented error, not a crash and not silent success
A captured run showing that after freeing all M blocks, a subsequent full set of M allocations succeeds
MEASURE.md reporting block size, block count, total pool bytes, and peak live blocks for a scripted pattern
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: After M successful allocations, allocation M+1 returns the documented OOM code and a null or invalid handle; both the code and the handle are shown in a captured run.
Double-free of the same block returns a documented error (not a crash, not a second successful free).
Freeing all M live blocks allows a following sequence of M allocations to succeed; the captured run prints success for that refill.
MEASURE.md states integers for block size S, block count M, total pool bytes, and peak live blocks for one named scripted pattern (for example allocate all, free every other, allocate again).
